ciderlight.settings.title: Ciderlight Settings
ciderlight.settings.button.tooltip: Shaders, shadows, waving plants, water reflections, ambient occlusion, lighting brightness and the world's render scale.
ciderlight.tooltip.shaders: Ciderlight's shadows, light shafts, water, sky and waving plants. Off keeps the Metal renderer with Minecraft's own look.
ciderlight.tooltip.quality: How much the shaders cost on the GPU. Low has smaller shadow maps, coarser fog, lighter water reflections and draws the world at two thirds of the window's resolution; it is what A-series chips and the plain M1 to M4 start on. High is what everything else starts on. The quality is kept while the shaders are off.
ciderlight.tooltip.render_scale: The world's resolution as a share of the window's; the HUD and menus stay sharp. Lower is faster. Auto: two thirds on Low, full on High. Applies immediately.
ciderlight.tooltip.shadows: The sun and moon cast shadows, and light shafts form in the haze. Off skips the shadow maps, the biggest single cost on the GPU, and lights everything as if it stood in the open.
ciderlight.tooltip.waving: Leaves, grass, flowers and crops sway in the wind.
ciderlight.tooltip.water_reflections: Water mirrors the hills, trees and buildings around it. Off: water reflects the sky only, which costs less.
ciderlight.tooltip.water_waves: Waves roll across lakes and the sea and run down waterfalls. Off: the water lies calm (rain still ripples it).
ciderlight.tooltip.ao: Soft shade in corners, under ledges and between blocks.
ciderlight.tooltip.ambient_light: How much light shaded and unlit surfaces get: the brightness of caves, night and shadows. Above 100% lifts the darkness; 0% leaves only direct sunlight and torches.
ciderlight.tooltip.sunlight: How bright direct sunlight (and moonlight) is on surfaces. 100% is the tuned look; above it sunlit faces get brighter, below it they fall towards the shaded colour.
ciderlight.tooltip.shadow_darkness: How much sunlight a shadow takes away. 0% draws no shadow darkening, 100% is the tuned look, above that shadows go darker than the tuned look.
ciderlight.tooltip.torch_light: How bright torches, lanterns, lava and other block light are. 100% is the tuned look.
ciderlight.tooltip.exposure: Overall image brightness, applied at the very end of the composite.
ciderlight.tooltip.saturation: How strong the colours are. 0% is greyscale; 100% is the tuned look.
ciderlight.tooltip.explosion_light: How brightly an explosion lights the world around it. 0% turns the burst off; 100% is the tuned look. A burning fuse's blink does not light the world, only the blast does.
ciderlight.note.apply: Click Apply to use this setting
ciderlight.note.forced: Set by -Dciderlight.%s in the JVM arguments
